what: a loft from a 40 square at z=0 to a circle r10 at z=30
method: two sections loft ruled; the circle is split at the square's corner directions (45 deg + k 90 deg) into four quarter arcs, and each side is ruled to its arc at equal parameter (the side's linear one, the arc's standard rational quadratic, weights 1, cos45, 1). A section at height s h is the curve (1-s) C0 + s C1, whose area is (1-s)^2 A0 + 2 s (1-s) M + s^2 A1 (M = 1/4 loop int (C0 x dC1 + C1 x dC0), Gauss) = 716.895118350: V = h (A0 + M + A1)/3, z_c = h (A0/12 + M/6 + A1/4) / ((A0 + M + A1)/3), A0 = 1600, A1 = 100 pi. (Pairing the side with the arc by its angle instead gives M = 720.2, V 0.13% more; by the arc's weights 727.1, 0.39% more.) Faces: the two caps and four ruled sides; edges 4 + 4 + the four rulings from the corners; vertices 4 + 4; on the axis by the four-fold symmetry
